title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Discount a Settlement Record Carries on a Block Purchase
content:
*When does a discount come off the price of a block?*

Where the payments received in the ledger window of 12 months cover what was invoiced in it and no open
position stands on the program, a discount of 2.0 percent comes off. Where those payments cover what was
invoiced in it and an open position does stand, a discount of 1.0 percent comes off. In any other case
no discount comes off for the account's settlement record.

*What is read over that window?* The charges invoiced on the rate program with a due day falling in the
12 months to the day of the purchase, and the payments received on the program in the same 12 months.
The open position is read over the whole life of the program rather than over that window.

| Payments in the 12-month window against what it invoiced | The open position on the program | The discount |
|---|---|---|
| cover it | none stands | 2.0 percent |
| cover it | one stands | 1.0 percent |
| fall short of it | any | no discount comes off |

*An illustration.* A rate program under the Demand Service Rate Programs whose window invoiced 12000 US
dollars and received 12000 US dollars, with nothing owed over the life of the program, carries the
discount of 2.0 percent; the same window with 500 US dollars still owed over the life of the program
carries 1.0 percent. A window that invoiced 12000 US dollars against 9000 US dollars received carries no
discount at all.
